title: Ethics in Daily Life
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper

Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

questions.answer: C

questions.answer: A

questions.answer: A

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: Read the paragraph and answer. Priya is always on time for her shift at the hospital, is polite, follows all safety procedures and never discusses patients' details with outsiders. Which four work ethics is Priya following?
questions.answer: Regularity and punctuality; politeness (cordial relations); following rules and procedures (safety); confidentiality.

questions.q: Read the paragraph. Neha is always on time for work, completes her tasks sincerely and respects her colleagues. Sam is often late, ignores his work and greets nobody. State True or False. (i) Neha is sincere and cooperative. (ii) Sam is very responsible and disciplined.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False: Sam is irresponsible and undisciplined.

questions.q: Name any two examples of general ethics. State any two examples of work ethics.
questions.answer: General ethics: sincerity and honesty (also truthfulness, respect for time). Work ethics: regularity and punctuality, and confidentiality (also loyalty).

questions.q: Which four codes of ethics should be followed in a school?
questions.answer: Be regular and punctual; be polite and respectful to teachers and classmates; do your own work without copying or cheating; do not waste school resources and follow school rules.

questions.q: Separate the following as general ethics and work ethics: regularity, sincerity, punctuality, loyalty, confidentiality, self-respect, respect for the environment, truthfulness.
questions.answer: General ethics: sincerity, self-respect, respect for the environment, truthfulness. Work ethics: regularity, punctuality, loyalty, confidentiality.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What does the word 'ethics' deal with?
questions.answer: It deals with moral issues and with right and wrong behaviour. Ethics tell us our moral duties so that behaviour at home and work is right, truthful and just.

or.q: Name any two examples of general ethics.
or.answer: Sincerity and honesty are general ethics. Truthfulness and respect for time are also general ethics.

questions.q: Name four work ethics expected of a doctor.
questions.answer: A doctor should be regular and punctual, keep patients' information confidential, be polite and sympathetic, and keep learning to update knowledge and skills.

or.q: Mention four work ethics expected of a student.
or.answer: A student should be regular and punctual, do her own work honestly without copying, respect teachers and classmates, and be willing to learn.

questions.q: List four unethical behaviours commonly seen on the road.
questions.answer: Jumping the queue or signal and breaking traffic rules. Rude behaviour, bribing officials and misuse of vehicles.

or.q: Which four ethical qualities do you expect from your boss?
or.answer: Fairness without favouritism, honesty, politeness and respect for all workers, and loyalty to the organisation.

questions.q: Why should ethics be taught in schools and colleges?
questions.answer: Values become habits when learnt early and habits are hard to give up. It helps to make disciplined citizens who do their work efficiently.

questions.q: What is a code of ethics? Give one example of a rule from it.
questions.answer: It is a list of clear rules and principles to guide behaviour at home and at work. For example, be regular and punctual at work and at home.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain any three ethical problems commonly faced at the workplace.
questions.answer: (i) Irregularity and lack of punctuality, which spoils discipline and causes inconvenience to the public. (ii) Wastage of resources such as lights, fans, stationery and vehicles. (iii) Disloyalty such as selling company secrets, taking bribes or cheating the employer.

questions.q: How can ethical standards be raised? (three points)
questions.answer: (i) Public disclosure and publicity so that corrupt workers are held responsible. (ii) Preparing and displaying a code of ethics so that expectations are known. (iii) Teaching ethics and moral values in schools and colleges from an early age.

questions.q: Your brother makes excuses for not helping at home. How will you explain that his habit is wrong?
questions.answer: (i) Tell him that sharing work is a family duty and honesty in work is an ethic. (ii) Explain that excuses show irresponsibility and disrespect for work and family. (iii) Encourage him with a daily work list and appreciate his help.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the three components of a work situation and why the worker is the most important. Give a code of ethics for good living (five points).
questions.answer: (i) A work situation has work (the task), the worker and the work place. (ii) The worker is the most important because only a worker can think, learn and manage. (iii) Be regular and punctual and do the assigned task. (iv) Be polite, acquire knowledge and skills and keep learning. (v) Do not waste resources, follow rules uniformly and avoid favouritism or discrimination. (vi) Be loyal, respect all work and expose corruption.
